ai.description: This 30–60 cm snake is iridescent dark brown to purplish-black with a yellow-spotted belly. It has a blunt, cylindrical body, tiny eyes, and a flattened, spine-tipped tail. Family: Uropeltidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Nilgiri Burrowing Snake is best identified by the presence of a distinct, sharp, spine-like scale at the very tip of its tail, which is absent in other similar species.
ai.habitat: The Nilgiri burrowing snake inhabits high-altitude montane grasslands and shola forests in the Nilgiri Hills, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Nilgiri burrowing snake is primarily nocturnal and spends most of its time underground, surfacing mainly after heavy rains to hunt earthworms.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Plectrurus perroteti* is ovoviviparous, giving birth to a small litter of 3–5 live young. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Nilgiri burrowing snake is endemic to the high-elevation grasslands and shola forests of the Western Ghats in Tamil Nadu and Kerala, typically above 1,500 meters.
